served.stem: A woman who is red-green colorblind has children with a man who has normal color vision. Red-green color blindness is X-linked recessive. What is expected among their children?
choices: All daughters affected and all sons unaffected
All sons affected, all daughters carriers
served.bankWhy: An affected mother carries the colorblind allele on both of her X chromosomes, so every single child receives one copy from her. A son pairs that X with a Y and has nothing to mask it, so all sons are colorblind. A daughter pairs it with her father's normal X, so she sees color normally while carrying the allele. This criss-cross from mother to son is the classic X-linked recessive signature worth recognising on sight.

answer.text: All sons affected, all daughters carriers
answer.line: Both of the mother's X chromosomes carry the allele, so every child gets one. Sons have no second X to mask it.

steps: Write the parents first: he is X^N Y, and she is X^n X^n, with the allele on both X chromosomes.
Every child gets one X from her, and both of hers carry n. So every child gets an n.
Sons get the Y from him. X^n Y has nothing to mask the n, so every son is colorblind.
Daughters get his X^N, which covers the n. X^N X^n sees color normally and carries the allele.

choices.text: All daughters affected and all sons unaffected
choices.note: This flips who gets what. The father gives each daughter his normal X, which covers the allele, and gives each son only a Y.
One in four is the autosomal carrier by carrier cross, where each parent passes the allele by chance. Here the mother passes it to every child.
Normal vision is true of the daughters. A son takes his only X from his mother, and both of hers carry the allele.
Masking needs a second allele. Sons have one X, so nothing covers the recessive allele, and every daughter still carries it.

choices.text: All sons affected, all daughters carriers
choices.note: Sons: X^n from her plus his Y. Daughters: X^n from her plus his X^N.
